'''Campeón de Campeones''' is a professional [[association football]] competition in [[Mexico]] and a domestic [[super cup]] contested by the [[Liga MX]] champions of the ''Apertura'' and ''Clausura'' tournaments. Until 1995, it was contested by the league and cup champions. Since 2018, the winners have also competed in the [[Campeones Cup]],<ref name="Major League Soccer">{{cite press release |date=March 13, 2018 |title=Major League Soccer and Liga MX Fuel Rivalry with New Partnership |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2018/03/13/major-league-soccer-and-liga-mx-fuel-rivalry-new-partnership |publisher=[[Major League Soccer]] |access-date=March 13, 2018}}</ref> facing the [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] champions.

The trophy has been contested in 52 editions, the inaugural year in the professional era was played in 1943 with [[C.D. Marte|Marte]] crowned as the first champions.

Eighteen clubs have been champions at least once. [[Club América|América]] and [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]] are the most successful clubs with seven titles each, [[Club León|León]], [[Toluca FC|Toluca]] and [[Atlas F.C.|Atlas]] with five titles each.

==History==
===Amateur era===
The Campeón de Campeones was created in 1942, one edition was played corresponding to the amateur era of Mexican football. The trophy was contested by [[Real Club España]] the Liga Mayor champions and [[Atlante F.C.|Atlante]] the Copa México champions of the 1941–42 season, with Atlante winning the trophy 5–4 on aggregate.  

===Professional era===
The beginning of the professional era of the Campeón de Campeones was established in 1943. The trophy was presented by the president of Mexico at the time, [[Manuel Ávila Camacho]]. From 1942 to 1995 the tournament was contested between the [[Liga MX]] champions and the [[Copa MX]] champions.  Traditionally the single match (with an exception in 1968 and 1988 when two matches were played) to determine the trophy winners was held at the end of the season at a stadium in Mexico City.

If a club won the league and cup titles of the same year, they were awarded the title ''Campeonísimo'' with an automatic awarding of the Campeón de Campeones trophy. To date this has only occurred on five occasions ([[Club León|León]]  in 1949, [[Cruz Azul]] in 1969, [[C.D. Guadalajara|Guadalajara]] in 1970, [[Club Puebla|Puebla]] in 1990, and [[Club Necaxa|Necaxa]] in 1995).

After 1995 the league championship was split into two shorter seasons [[Apertura and Clausura]]. Then in 1997, the [[Mexican Football Federation|FMF]] canceled the cup tournament. Due to these changes, the ''Campeón de Campeones'' was postponed. The competition resumed in the 2002–03 season; however, this time it was contested between the champions of Apertura and Clausura. The competition was held four times and was placed on hiatus again from 2007 to 2014.

In 2012, an unofficial match was played between the Liga MX champions and the Ascenso MX champions, [[Club León|Leon]] beat [[Santos Laguna]] 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aztecadeportes.com/notas/futbol-mexicano/121042/leon-gana-el-campeon-de-campeones-a-santos|title=León gana el Campeón de Campeones a Santos|date=8 July 2012|access-date=2012-09-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131226003135/http://www.aztecadeportes.com/notas/futbol-mexicano/121042/leon-gana-el-campeon-de-campeones-a-santos|archive-date=2013-12-26|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/mexico/noticias/2012/07/08/santos-0-2-leon-la-fiera-esta-incontenible|title=Santos 0–2 León... La Fiera está incontenible|date=8 July 2012|access-date=27 May 2013|archive-date=2 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702122352/http://www.mediotiempo.com/futbol/mexico/noticias/2012/07/08/santos-0-2-leon-la-fiera-esta-incontenible|url-status=live}}</ref> In the 2013–14 season, the Liga MX stipulated that a Campeón de Campeones match should be contested between the champions of the Apertura 2013 and Copa MX Apertura 2013,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.femexfut.org.mx/portalv2/docs/reglamentos/new/COMPETENCIA/Reglamento_de_Competencia_LIGA_MX.pdf|title=Reglamento de competencia Liga MX 2012–2013|page=52|access-date=2013-05-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131225215651/http://www.femexfut.org.mx/portalv2/docs/reglamentos/new/COMPETENCIA/Reglamento_de_Competencia_LIGA_MX.pdf|archive-date=2013-12-25|url-status=dead}}</ref> but it was not officially disputed.

==Competition format==
The format was changed to a single match at a neutral site, which is in the United States and shared with the [[Supercopa MX]] match, and the team with the higher aggregate table points across both Apertura and Clausura tournaments is declared the designated "home" team.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gomez |first=Eric |date=September 13, 2017 |title=Monday Night Fútbol? Five ways to solve Liga MX's TV problem |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/mexican-liga-mx/22/blog/post/3203059/five-ways-to-fix-liga-mx-tv-problem |publisher=ESPN |access-date=May 22, 2018 |archive-date=May 23, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180523173008/http://www.espn.com/soccer/mexican-liga-mx/22/blog/post/3203059/five-ways-to-fix-liga-mx-tv-problem |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |date=June 5, 2015 |title=Toyota Stadium selected to host American debut of Campeón de Campeones and SuperCopa with July 20 doubleheader |url=https://www.fcdallas.com/post/2015/06/05/toyota-stadium-selected-host-american-debut-campe%C3%B3n-de-campeones-and-supercopa-july |publisher=[[FC Dallas]] |access-date=May 22, 2018}}</ref>
In 2015, the [[Liga MX]] restarted the Campeón de Campeones with the match between [[Santos Laguna]] and [[Club América|América]], the match was played at a neutral venue ([[Toyota Stadium (Texas)|Toyota Stadium]] in [[Frisco, Texas]]), that was the first edition of the competition that was played in the United States. 

Similarly to the traditional tournament, if a team wins both the Apertura and Clausura seasons, the team is automatically awarded the Campeón de Campeones trophy. This has occurred twice, [[Atlas F.C.|Atlas]] in 2022 for winning the 2021 Apertura and the 2022 Clausura. [[Club América]] in 2024 for winning the 2023 Apertura and the 2024 Clausura.
